title.narrative: Listening Dialogues on Climate and Migration - JLI

description.narrative:
“Listening Dialogues” are a methodology developed and piloted by JLI as part of its Fair & Equitable Approach, and the foundation upon which JLI has created five regional interdisciplinary learning hubs. They are facilitated discussion workshops which can either be conducted online, or face-to-face.The purpose of the Listening Dialogues would be to bring together local faith actors, humanitarian and development practitioners, and researchers to meet the following objectives:
Create a fair and equitable reflective discussion space Review the current state of evidence on the role of religion and faith actors in preparing for or responding to climate-induced migration Consider who has been leading current evidence agendas, and whether these reflect the priorities and experiences of local communities Define evidence priorities and needs on climate-induced migration to inform practice and policy, and how organisations like JLI and Christian Aid can support community-led evidence agendas
